title: General doctor visit
what: The first doctor to see. They ask questions, examine you, prescribe treatment, or refer you to a specialist.
why: When something bothers you and you are not sure which doctor to see. Also for checkups, medical certificates, and long-term illnesses.
tell_doctor: What bothers you and since when
What medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take

prepare.title: Your concerns
prepare.text: Write down what bothers you and what you want to ask. It is easy to forget during the visit.

prepare.title: Blood pressure
prepare.text: If you check your blood pressure or blood sugar at home, bring your records.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable, so your chest and arm are easy to uncover for a blood pressure check.

bring: Past test results, medical records, and reports
A list of your medicines or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your concerns and your health
They check your blood pressure and pulse, and sometimes your temperature and weight
They listen to your heart and lungs
They look at your throat and feel your belly
They explain what comes next: treatment, tests, or another doctor
feel: Nothing unpleasant. It is a normal checkup
after: The doctor gives you prescriptions and referrals
If something is unclear, ask while you are still in the room
Do not change your treatment on your own. If you have questions, ask your doctor
red_flags: Chest pain, shortness of breath, a drooping face, weakness in an arm or leg, or a sudden severe headache: do not wait for the visit. Call emergency services

faq.q: How do I prepare for a visit to a general doctor?
faq.a: Write down your concerns and questions, make a list of your medicines, and bring past test results. The visit will be quicker and more useful.

faq.q: Do I need to see a general doctor before a specialist?
faq.a: Often yes. The general doctor works out which specialist you need and orders the right tests straight away.
